answer: Each agent must stake copper tokens to join, and stake is slashed if peer review flags duplicate identities. At the mesa summit, validators randomly audit a sample of agents quarterly, requiring live proof-of-work tied to unique hardware. A sybil attacker would need to acquire and maintain many distinct staked identities plus pass audits, making the cost of forging N identities far exceed the reward, so legitimate agents stay profitable.
